audit.summary: The excerpt provided is almost entirely Part II boilerplate with no operating MD&A, so revenue, margin and cash flow trends cannot be verified — but what is disclosed paints the picture of a bitcoin-treasury vehicle rather than an operating business: management cash bonuses are keyed to 'Bitcoin Yield' and PSUs to TSR versus bitcoin, while two amended-and-restated ATM sales agreements with eight banks stand ready to issue equity continuously. audit.summary: MPC posted a spectacular quarter ($17.73 diluted EPS vs $3.96) but the overwhelming majority of the improvement is cyclical crack-spread expansion tied to Middle East supply disruption — management itself attributes ~$4 billion of the quarterly margin gain to market indicators alone, and throughput actually fell 116 mbpd with utilization down to 94%. Underlying quality is softer than the headline: unit operating, distribution and turnaround costs all rose, RIN expense more than doubled, the fee-based Midstream segment was essentially flat for the half despite acquisitions, a large slice of record operating cash flow was reversible working capital, and the SPR exchange obligates MPC to return ~27 million barrels against ~22 million received. Offsetting this are real positives: ~$800M of company-specific margin over-capture, a cash balance that more than doubled to $7.77 billion, an extended 2031 revolver, a profitable Renewable Diesel business, and an incremental $5 billion buyback authorization.

audit.summary: Arcosa's headline numbers look stable, but the quality underneath is uneven: consolidated revenue grew only 1.7% in the quarter with organic aggregates and asphalt volumes declining, Construction Products operating profit fell 6-9%, and the eye-catching 46% jump in Engineered Structures profit was roughly one-fifth attributable to a one-time Mexican land sale gain. Cash generation is the biggest concern — $33.4 million of six-month operating cash flow against $102.3 million of capex and a $166.3 million working capital drain — while GAAP net income is optically flattered by the $359.7 million barge divestiture gain and rising tax rates signal the AMP credit tailwind is fading alongside a structurally shrinking wind tower business. Offsetting this are a legitimately strong 49% year-to-date increase in utility structures backlog tied to grid and AI-driven power demand, real gross margin expansion in Engineered Structures, and deleveraging; however, the pending $150/share CRH merger now dominates the equity story and imposes operating restrictions plus a $260.4 million break fee.

red_flags.evidence: Total backlog fell to $22,136M at July 31, 2026 from $22,622M at January 30, 2026 (negotiated unfunded backlog $18,318M vs $19,050M; Civilian $4,003M vs $4,242M). Net bookings of $1.2B in Q2 against $1,880M of revenue implies a ~0.64 book-to-bill (~0.87 for the six months).

audit.summary: SAIC posted respectable headline growth (6% in Q2, ~5.3% organic) and strong GAAP margin expansion, but the GAAP improvement is flattered by easy prior-year comparisons ($7M tax-audit settlement costs) and a $12M investment gain that management left inside its 'adjusted' operating income and EBITDA — on an adjusted basis Q2 margins actually slipped (10.3%→10.2% operating, 10.5%→10.3% EBITDA). The bigger concern is demand: total backlog fell sequentially to $22.1B from $22.6B with an implied Q2 book-to-bill near 0.64, cost mix is shifting toward lower-margin materials content, and 97% government exposure leaves the company hostage to the September 30, 2026 funding cliff and unresolved ICE/CBP appropriations. Cash flow improved but was driven by vendor-payment timing and lower incentive comp rather than better collections.
